evidence.claim: Given limited visibility below tier two and political pressure around domestic sourcing, qualified lower-tier aerospace suppliers with compliant materials, certifications, quality records, and on-time delivery could become economically important even if prime-level aircraft or engine demand is unchanged.

node: Domestic-content aerospace and defense components: castings, forgings, precision machining, alloys, fasteners, and engine subcomponents
summary: This pass expands the universe around qualified U.S.-listed aerospace and defense component suppliers that could benefit if political, tariff, Buy American, or Pentagon sourcing pressure forces OEMs and primes to requalify suppliers with stronger domestic-content documentation, aerospace certifications, quality records, and delivery performance. The underfollowed angle is strongest below the prime/OEM layer: specialty alloy producers, forgings/castings suppliers, fastener makers, and precision component manufacturers may become chokepoints because aerospace qualification cycles, NADCAP/AS9100 processes, raw-material traceability, and capacity constraints can slow substitution. Evidence is still early and uneven; most company-specific links below are Layer 1 hypotheses requiring filing-level verification.
